title: Editorial Policy
description: How SignalNest discovers, drafts, reviews, approves, corrects and retires articles.
heading: Editorial Policy
body:
This policy governs every article on SignalNest. It exists so that readers can judge how a piece of writing was produced.

1. What we publish

SignalNest publishes content that is useful to a specific reader with a specific problem. Before a draft is accepted it must be accurate, original, practically useful, clearly explained, supported by sources where it makes factual claims, readable, and matched to real search or reader intent.

2. No automatic publishing

Drafts may be produced with AI assistance. No draft is published by the same process that wrote it. Publication requires a named human editor to read the draft and record an explicit approval. The publishing system refuses any article without that recorded approval, and the approval is verified server-side rather than by a button in a browser.

3. Human verification is required for

  • Statistics, percentages and study findings
  • Legal and regulatory statements
  • Financial information, including prices, fees and rates
  • Medical and health claims
  • Product specifications and feature claims
  • Breaking news and anything time-sensitive

Where a claim cannot be verified, it is removed or described as unverified. It is never silently kept.

4. Sources

Articles cite primary sources where possible: official documentation, published research, regulator notices, or the vendor's own specification page. Every published article lists its sources with an access date. Sources are linked, not described.

5. What we never do

  • Fabricate research, quotations, expert opinions or first-hand experience.
  • Publish spun, rewritten or duplicated content to attract search traffic.
  • Stuff keywords or repeat paragraphs to inflate length.
  • Present a generated passage as a personal anecdote.
  • Accept payment for a favourable verdict.

6. Advertising separation

Advertising appears in labelled containers outside the article body. Ads are never styled to look like editorial recommendations, and no article instructs readers to click an ad.

7. Corrections and retirement

Substantive corrections are made in place and the updated date changes. When an article no longer reflects reality and cannot be repaired, it is removed or redirected rather than left to mislead. Corrections are logged with a timestamp.

8. AI transparency

Where a language model contributed to a draft, the article metadata records the model and generation date. This is disclosed so readers can weigh the source appropriately.
